title: Garments & Armor
notes: This chunk builds a dense, law-positive case that the wedding garment is the righteous acts of the covenant, chaining Genesis skins, Ezekiel covering, Isaiah robes, and Revelation linen with clean Greek notes and tight cross-references. Strengths include the given-then-worn distinction, the filthy-rags correction, the baptism-plus-feet typology, and the deliberate AI-pulpit contrast. Issues are multiple house-style violations of sentence-initial And/But/That in author prose, one residual presenter cue (“Now run”), and a slightly loose relative clause on the kanaph. No doctrine, quote, or math errors appear. Surgical openers and staging fixes restore compliance while preserving voice and density.

This chunk chains Isaiah’s war-dress through David, the mitre, forehead seals, Saul’s failed assay, and Paul’s list into the marriage garment with high density and a law-positive close. The yeshuah helmet, light-pun, and symbol inventory land cleanly. Four author-prose sentences open with And/But, two director cues remain (Mark the weight; Now walk down), one hedging clause softens the armour-of-God claim, and a modern fitting-room metaphor jars the duel image. Surgical removals restore house style without touching doctrine or quoted text.

proposals.old: But the word is plural and active — righteous _acts_.
proposals.new: The word is plural and active — righteous _acts_.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences starting with But.

proposals.old: And it is the robe the father calls for when the prodigal comes home: __“Bring forth the *best robe*, and put it on him”__ (Luke 15:22) — the covenant covering restored on repentance, before the boy can finish his speech.
proposals.new: It is the robe the father calls for when the prodigal comes home: __“Bring forth the *best robe*, and put it on him”__ (Luke 15:22) — the covenant covering restored on repentance, before the boy can finish his speech.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences starting with And.

proposals.old: That spread skirt is the _kanaph_, the sym:sym-wings[wing], link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[doing both of its offices]: the edge that carries the fringe bound as the reminder to keep the commandments and do them (Numbers 15:39), and the shade a refuge shelters under.footnote:fn37kanaph[The kanaph — wing, skirt, border, corner — and the fringe at its edge are derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.]
proposals.new: The spread skirt is the _kanaph_, the sym:sym-wings[wing], link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[doing both of its offices]: the edge that carries the fringe bound as the reminder to keep the commandments and do them (Numbers 15:39), and the shade a refuge shelters under.footnote:fn37kanaph[The kanaph — wing, skirt, border, corner — and the fringe at its edge are derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.]
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences starting with That.

proposals.old: But read the whole line: __“we are all as an unclean thing,”__ and so even __“our righteousnesses”__ come out stained.
proposals.new: The whole line: __“we are all as an unclean thing,”__ and so even __“our righteousnesses”__ come out stained.
proposals.summary: Remove But and residual director cue.
proposals.rationale: House style bars sentence-initial But and director cues such as Read that; the claim stands without the staging.

proposals.old: And __“ye also ought to wash one another’s feet”__ (John 13:14).
proposals.new: __“ye also ought to wash one another’s feet”__ (John 13:14).
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences starting with And; the quoted clause stands cleanly.

proposals.old: And Paul’s one dread for the day of resurrection is to be caught uncovered — __“if so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked”__ (2 Corinthians 5:3).
proposals.new: Paul’s one dread for the day of resurrection is to be caught uncovered — __“if so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked”__ (2 Corinthians 5:3).
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences starting with And.

proposals.old: Now run the words through the whole of Scripture instead.
proposals.new: The words run through the whole of Scripture instead.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids director cues of the form Now watch / Now derive / Now run; the re-reading claim is stronger as assertion.

proposals.old: The armor is God's own war-dress, put on because no man could — which is what __“the whole armour *of God*”__ (Ephesians 6:11) says when it is allowed to mean it: not armor from His stores, but the armor He wears, lent to the soldier.
proposals.new: The armor is God's own war-dress, put on because no man could — which is what __“the whole armour *of God*”__ (Ephesians 6:11) says: not armor from His stores, but the armor He wears, lent to the soldier.
proposals.rationale: “When it is allowed to mean it” is meta-talk that softens the assertion; the claim stands stronger without it.

proposals.old: And the Hebrew under __“salvation”__ is the word this book met on the mountains of the link:/books/symbolic-language/gospel/[Gospel] chapter: _yeshuah_ — the helmet of *Yeshuah*.
proposals.new: The Hebrew under __“salvation”__ is the word this book met on the mountains of the link:/books/symbolic-language/gospel/[Gospel] chapter: _yeshuah_ — the helmet of *Yeshuah*.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with And; the sentence stands complete without it.

proposals.old: And what covers a man's head? __“the *head* of every man is *Christ*”__ (1 Corinthians 11:3).
proposals.new: What covers a man's head? __“the *head* of every man is *Christ*”__ (1 Corinthians 11:3).
proposals.rationale: House style forbids And at the start of author prose; the question needs no conjunction.

proposals.old: Scripture even stages the two armors side by side, in a fitting room before a duel.
proposals.new: Scripture sets the two armors side by side before a duel.
proposals.rationale: “Fitting room” is anachronistic retail language that fights the biblical armor-and-duel frame; “sets” keeps the parallel cleanly.
“Mark the weight” is a forbidden presenter cue; a short declarative matches the chapter’s other one-line seals.

proposals.old: Now walk down Paul's whole list with the Glossary of this book open: the girdle of sym:sym-truth[truth], the breastplate of sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness], the feet shod with the sym:sym-gospel[gospel] of sym:sym-peace[peace], the shield of sym:sym-faith[faith], the helmet of _yeshuah_, and the sym:sym-sword[sword] of the Spirit, __“which is the *word of God*”__ (Ephesians 6:17).
proposals.new: Paul's whole list, matched to the Glossary of this book, is the girdle of sym:sym-truth[truth], the breastplate of sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness], the feet shod with the sym:sym-gospel[gospel] of sym:sym-peace[peace], the shield of sym:sym-faith[faith], the helmet of _yeshuah_, and the sym:sym-sword[sword] of the Spirit, __“which is the *word of God*”__ (Ephesians 6:17).
proposals.rationale: Director cue violates house style; the revised lead asserts the match without instructing the reader.

proposals.old: But __“many are called… few are chosen”__ (Matthew 22:14): the chosen are the few found on the sym:sym-highway[highway] of holiness, properly dressed.
proposals.new: Yet __“many are called… few are chosen”__ (Matthew 22:14): the chosen are the few found on the sym:sym-highway[highway] of holiness, properly dressed.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with But; Yet preserves the contrast without the forbidden starter.

proposals.old: And how a covenant binds not one wearer but a whole people together is the next symbol: the bow.
proposals.new: How a covenant binds not one wearer but a whole people together is the next symbol: the bow.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids And at the start of author prose; the forward link stands without it.
